messages.subject: adivice with distsamp and backTransform
parts:
Good morning to all,

I want to test if several categorical and non categorical variables related to habitat affect the abundance of my species. Therefore, I am fitting models with different combinations of these variables. But I have some questions (some related to errors). 

1) What id the model with the lowest AIC is the null mode? Should I choose the best model based solely on AIC?
2) When trying to fit a model with only one covariate, I get the following error: Error: objeto de tipo 'symbol' no es subconjunto. Is it possible to fit models with only one covariate?
3) I already have fitted some models that include categorical and continuos variables. However I am not very sure in how to handle these when using backTransform (because of the categorical variables). What value should I enter to request the value of sigma? Should I use a different function/approach?

Thank you very much for your answer. An answer to any of those questions will greatly help me. I am very new to unmarked and these analyses!

Laura

Best regards  --  Marc
From: unma...@googlegroups.com [unma...@googlegroups.com] on behalf of Laura Cespedes [lncespe...@gmail.com]
Sent: 28 June 2016 13:25
To: unmarked
Subject: [unmarked] adivice with distsamp and backTransform

Good morning to all,

I want to test if several categorical and non categorical variables related to habitat affect the abundance of my species. Therefore, I am fitting models with different combinations of these variables. But I have some questions (some related to errors).
1) What id the model with the lowest AIC is the null mode? Should I choose the best model based solely on AIC?

Yes, there is nothing wrong with the Null model. But note that model selection is a huge field and there are quite different opinions about whether and how it should be done (see for instance the paper by ver Hoef and Boveng who argue that inferences on a single model may sometimes be preferrable: http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jwmg.891/abstract).
2) When trying to fit a model with only one covariate, I get the following error: Error: objeto de tipo 'symbol' no es subconjunto. Is it possible to fit models with only one covariate?

Yes, it is, absolutely. I think that this error may have to do with different patterns of missing values in your covariates. When you fit models with different covariates and you want to compare them using AIC, then you must use exactly the same data set. However, if there are NA's at different places in the covariates, then depending on which model (with which covariates) you fit, you will end up using different data sets, and the AIC will no longer be comparable for these models. The solution is to restrict, from the beginning, the data set that you feed into unmarked (via the unmarked data frame) such that you always use the same data, regardless of the covariates that are included in a model.

3) I already have fitted some models that include categorical and continuos variables. However I am not very sure in how to handle these when using backTransform (because of the categorical variables). What value should I enter to request the value of sigma? Should I use a different function/approach?

When you predict for a fitted model object obtained using distsamp or gdistamp, you must choose whether which level of the hierarchical model you want the predictions for: the state (abundance or density) or the observation (the detection function). When you choose one, then the regression equation for the other one is irrelevant. So, if you want to predict abundance or density (i.e., the state), you don't need to worry about sigma.
Have you looked at the distance sampling vignette (available here: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/unmarked/index.html), in sections 4 and 5 ?

Thank you very much for your answer. An answer to any of those questions will greatly help me. I am very new to unmarked and these analyses!

Laura

#Dynamic Model (DP is a quadratic function of Dayscore (May 15th))
